title: Version cadence oracle and gatekeeper tooling for runtime compatibility
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: Our runtime receives frequent changes that interact in subtle ways with public and internal client adapters. Historically we've relied on manual reviews and ad-hoc migration notes for breaking changes, which has caused last-minute rollbacks and customer confusion during LTS rollouts.

Goal: Define a lightweight but enforceable semantic versioning cadence and implement an automated 'Gatekeeper' tool + dashboard that (a) computes a compatibility score for proposed changes, (b) recommends a semver bump and LTS channel target, and (c) wires into CI to block merges that don't meet policy or lack migration steps. This reduces manual overhead, standardizes communication, and creates telemetry for future deprecation windows.

Scope: Policy covers the serving runtime public HTTP/gRPC endpoints, client adapter contracts (JS/Python), and feature flags that materially change runtime behavior. Internal admin endpoints and telemetry-only fields are out of scope for this ticket and will be enumerated in follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: A written semver cadence doc describing what constitutes MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH in the runtime surface and an LTS channel mapping (stable, extended).
A runnable Gatekeeper binary (CLI) that: computes a compatibility score from a diff, suggests semver bump, and returns pass/fail for CI with exit code and JSON output.
A CI integration that blocks merges to main if a proposed change is MAJOR without an approved migration plan label or signed-off exception.
A Console dashboard prototype that exposes compatibility telemetry for recent merges and aggregate compatibility trend over 90 days.
Automated tests that assert Gatekeeper decisions on a set of synthetic diffs (positive and negative cases).
implementation_plan: Draft semantic rules document and circulate to runtime, SDK, and platform teams for review (week 1).
Design Gatekeeper input format: git diff + optional schema annotations + reduction hooks for language-specific adapters (week 2).
Implement core analyzer that parses Protobuf/OpenAPI/handler signatures and computes a compatibility delta and score (week 3-4).
Build CLI wrapper and CI action; add gating logic to CircleCI/GitHub Actions for runtime repo (week 5).
Ship Console dashboard with minimal telemetry: decision_id, commit, score, rationale (week 6).
Run canary for two sprints: permissive mode (log-only), then enforcement mode (block) after sign-off.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Analyzer false-positives could block non-breaking commits. Mitigation: start in log-only mode and maintain an exceptions registry with human overrides.
Risk: Enforcement may slow developer velocity. Mitigation: lightweight exemptions API and clear migration templates to shorten remediation time.
Risk: Telemetry volume could be high. Mitigation: sample decisions for the first 30 days and aggregate on the console side before full instrumentation.
Risk: Ambiguous public contract boundaries. Mitigation: create a short canonical list of 'public surfaces' in the policy doc and iterate with SDK owners.
qa_plan: Unit tests for analyzer heuristics using positive/negative diffs.
End-to-end test that runs Gatekeeper in CI against a forked runtime repo and validates correct CI behavior.
Manual review of 10 recent merges to ensure Gatekeeper's historical score aligns with human judgment.
Smoke test of Console dashboard and sampling pipeline.
notes: Aim for explainability: Gatekeeper must return a short rationale string for each decision (e.g. 'removed handler /v1/stream -> MAJOR').
We will expose a '--dry-run --rationale' mode for PR authors to see decisions inline before pushing.
Policy must include a 90-day deprecation window for any behavior classified as MINOR->MAJOR change to allow client migration cycles.
